title: Para-ksm: Parallelized Memory Deduplication with Data Streaming Accelerator
problem: Traditional kernel samepage merging (KSM) sequentially scans and compares memory pages to identify duplicates, creating CPU bottlenecks that limit deduplication throughput and adoption. The sequential nature of page hashing and comparison prevents efficient utilization of modern hardware parallelism.
motivation: Memory deduplication can significantly reduce memory footprint in virtualized and containerized systems, but CPU overhead of traditional KSM makes it impractical for performance-critical workloads.
method: Para-ksm introduces a hardware data streaming accelerator that parallelizes memory page scanning, hashing, and comparison operations. The accelerator streams memory pages through specialized hardware that performs parallel page hash computations and duplicate detection. This offloads deduplication work from the CPU, reducing overhead while increasing deduplication throughput.
key_novelty: Using a dedicated data streaming accelerator to parallelize memory deduplication scanning, eliminating the CPU-bound sequential bottleneck inherent in traditional KSM.
contributions: Parallelized memory deduplication architecture with hardware acceleration
Data streaming accelerator design for efficient page hashing and duplicate detection
Significant speedup and reduced CPU overhead compared to kernel-based KSM
Framework for integrating specialized hardware into kernel memory management subsystem
